input: List the first and last names of all patients who live in Rookwood.
output: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE city = 'Rookwood'

input: Which providers specialise in Cardiology? Show their full names.
output: SELECT full_name FROM providers WHERE specialty = 'Cardiology'

input: Show the names of every room on the second floor.
output: SELECT name FROM rooms WHERE floor = 2

input: Which procedures take longer than 30 minutes? Show the procedure names.
output: SELECT name FROM procedures WHERE duration_minutes > 30

input: Show the ids of all appointments that were cancelled.
output: SELECT id FROM appointments WHERE status = 'cancelled'

input: Which providers are no longer active? Show their full names.
output: SELECT full_name FROM providers WHERE is_active = 0

input: List the name and base fee of every procedure with a base fee of at least 200.
output: SELECT name, base_fee FROM procedures WHERE base_fee >= 200

input: Which patients are on the Self-pay plan? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE insurance_plan = 'Self-pay'

input: Show the id and scheduled time of every appointment in March 2026.
output: SELECT id, scheduled_at FROM appointments WHERE scheduled_at LIKE '2026-03%'

input: Which rooms are therapy rooms? Show the room names.
output: SELECT name FROM rooms WHERE room_type = 'therapy'

input: List the names of procedures that need an imaging room.
output: SELECT name FROM procedures WHERE room_type = 'imaging'

input: Which patients were born before 1950? Show first name, last name and date of birth.
output: SELECT first_name, last_name, date_of_birth FROM patients WHERE date_of_birth < '1950-01-01'

input: Which providers were hired after the end of 2020? Show full name and hire date.
output: SELECT full_name, hired_on FROM providers WHERE hired_on > '2020-12-31'

input: Show the ids of appointments with a copay of zero.
output: SELECT id FROM appointments WHERE copay = 0

input: Which patients registered during 2026? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE registered_on LIKE '2026%'

input: List the id and scheduled time of every no-show appointment.
output: SELECT id, scheduled_at FROM appointments WHERE status = 'no-show'

input: Which procedures belong to the Dermatology specialty? Show the names.
output: SELECT name FROM procedures WHERE specialty = 'Dermatology'

input: Which patients live in Sable Point and are on the Harbor Plus plan? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE city = 'Sable Point' AND insurance_plan = 'Harbor Plus'

input: How many patients does the clinic have on file?
output: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patients

input: What is the average base fee across all procedures?
output: SELECT AVG(base_fee) FROM procedures

input: How many appointments have the status completed?
output: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed'

input: How many appointments are there for each status? Show the status and the count.
output: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM appointments GROUP BY status

input: Show the ids of appointments held in the room named Exam 1.
output: SELECT a.id FROM appointments a JOIN rooms r ON r.id = a.room_id WHERE r.name = 'Exam 1'

input: For every appointment that is still scheduled, show the appointment id and the provider's full name.
output: SELECT a.id, p.full_name FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE a.status = 'scheduled'

input: Show the distinct first and last names of patients who have at least one no-show appointment.
output: SELECT DISTINCT p.first_name, p.last_name FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = p.id WHERE a.status = 'no-show'

input: What is the total copay collected from completed appointments?
output: SELECT SUM(copay) FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed'

input: How many procedures are offered in each specialty? Show specialty and count.
output: SELECT specialty, COUNT(*) FROM procedures GROUP BY specialty

input: What is the longest procedure duration in minutes?
output: SELECT MAX(duration_minutes) FROM procedures

input: For appointments in January 2026, show the appointment id and the procedure name.
output: SELECT a.id, pr.name FROM appointments a JOIN procedures pr ON pr.id = a.procedure_id WHERE a.scheduled_at LIKE '2026-01%'

input: How many rooms are there on each floor? Show floor and count.
output: SELECT floor, COUNT(*) FROM rooms GROUP BY floor

input: Which procedures can be performed in the room named Therapy North? Show the procedure names.
output: SELECT pr.name FROM procedures pr JOIN rooms r ON r.room_type = pr.room_type WHERE r.name = 'Therapy North'

input: How many patients are on each insurance plan? Show plan and count.
output: SELECT insurance_plan, COUNT(*) FROM patients GROUP BY insurance_plan

input: Show the appointment id and copay for every appointment with Dr. Priya Sandoval.
output: SELECT a.id, a.copay FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE p.full_name = 'Dr. Priya Sandoval'

input: What is the earliest scheduled appointment time on the books?
output: SELECT MIN(scheduled_at) FROM appointments

input: Show the ids of appointments that used a room on the third floor.
output: SELECT a.id FROM appointments a JOIN rooms r ON r.id = a.room_id WHERE r.floor = 3

input: How many distinct patients have had at least one appointment?
output: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM appointments

input: How many appointments has each provider had? Show the provider's full name and the count, most appointments first, then by name.
output: SELECT p.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY n DESC, p.full_name

input: What is the total copay per insurance plan across all appointments? Show plan and total, highest total first.
output: SELECT pt.insurance_plan, SUM(a.copay) AS total FROM appointments a JOIN patients pt ON pt.id = a.patient_id GROUP BY pt.insurance_plan ORDER BY total DESC

input: Which procedures are booked most often? Show procedure name and number of appointments, descending by count then by name.
output: SELECT pr.name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN procedures pr ON pr.id = a.procedure_id GROUP BY pr.id ORDER BY n DESC, pr.name

input: How many appointments have taken place in each room? Show room name and count, ordered by room name.
output: SELECT r.name, COUNT(*) FROM appointments a JOIN rooms r ON r.id = a.room_id GROUP BY r.id ORDER BY r.name

input: For each provider specialty, how many completed appointments are there? Show specialty and count ordered by specialty.
output: SELECT p.specialty, COUNT(*) FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.specialty ORDER BY p.specialty

input: Show each city with the number of appointments made by patients from that city, largest count first, then by city name.
output: SELECT pt.city, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN patients pt ON pt.id = a.patient_id GROUP BY pt.city ORDER BY n DESC, pt.city

input: What is the average copay per provider? Show full name and average, from highest average to lowest, then by name.
output: SELECT p.full_name, AVG(a.copay) AS avg_copay FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY avg_copay DESC, p.full_name

input: For each room type, what is the total number of procedure minutes booked? Show room type and total minutes, largest first.
output: SELECT r.room_type, SUM(pr.duration_minutes) AS minutes FROM appointments a JOIN rooms r ON r.id = a.room_id JOIN procedures pr ON pr.id = a.procedure_id GROUP BY r.room_type ORDER BY minutes DESC

input: Which patients have cancelled appointments? Show first name, last name and the number of cancellations, most first, then by last name and first name.
output: SELECT pt.first_name, pt.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN patients pt ON pt.id = a.patient_id WHERE a.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY pt.id ORDER BY n DESC, pt.last_name, pt.first_name

input: For each month of 2026, how many appointments did Family Medicine providers have? Show the month as YYYY-MM and the count, in month order.
output: SELECT substr(a.scheduled_at, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE p.specialty = 'Family Medicine' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

input: For completed appointments, what is the total base fee of procedures performed by each provider? Show full name and total, highest first, then by name.
output: SELECT p.full_name, SUM(pr.base_fee) AS total FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id JOIN procedures pr ON pr.id = a.procedure_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY total DESC, p.full_name

input: Who are the ten busiest patients? Show first name, last name and appointment count, most first, breaking ties by patient id.
output: SELECT pt.first_name, pt.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN patients pt ON pt.id = a.patient_id GROUP BY pt.id ORDER BY n DESC, pt.id LIMIT 10

input: For each floor, how many appointments were held there? Show floor and count ordered by floor.
output: SELECT r.floor, COUNT(*) FROM appointments a JOIN rooms r ON r.id = a.room_id GROUP BY r.floor ORDER BY r.floor

input: How many appointments of each status did each room type see? Show room type, status and count, ordered by room type then status.
output: SELECT r.room_type, a.status, COUNT(*) FROM appointments a JOIN rooms r ON r.id = a.room_id GROUP BY r.room_type, a.status ORDER BY r.room_type, a.status

input: Which providers have the most no-shows? Show full name and no-show count, descending by count then by name.
output: SELECT p.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE a.status = 'no-show' GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY n DESC, p.full_name

input: What is the average procedure duration of booked appointments per procedure specialty? Show specialty and average, highest average first, then by specialty.
output: SELECT pr.specialty, AVG(pr.duration_minutes) AS avg_minutes FROM appointments a JOIN procedures pr ON pr.id = a.procedure_id GROUP BY pr.specialty ORDER BY avg_minutes DESC, pr.specialty

input: For each insurance plan, how many distinct patients had a completed appointment? Show plan and count ordered by plan name.
output: SELECT pt.insurance_plan, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.id) FROM appointments a JOIN patients pt ON pt.id = a.patient_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY pt.insurance_plan ORDER BY pt.insurance_plan

input: For each procedure that has been booked, what is the latest scheduled appointment time? Show procedure name and time ordered by procedure name.
output: SELECT pr.name, MAX(a.scheduled_at) FROM appointments a JOIN procedures pr ON pr.id = a.procedure_id GROUP BY pr.id ORDER BY pr.name

input: Which patients have never had an appointment? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT patient_id FROM appointments)

input: Which providers have more than twelve appointments? Show their full names.
output: SELECT p.full_name FROM providers p JOIN appointments a ON a.provider_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id HAVING COUNT(*) > 12

input: Which procedures cost more than the average base fee? Show name and base fee.
output: SELECT name, base_fee FROM procedures WHERE base_fee > (SELECT AVG(base_fee) FROM procedures)

input: Which patients have more than one appointment booked through the portal? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT pt.first_name, pt.last_name FROM patients pt JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = pt.id WHERE a.booked_via = 'portal' GROUP BY pt.id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

input: Which procedures have never had a cancelled appointment? Show the procedure names.
output: SELECT name FROM procedures WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT procedure_id FROM appointments WHERE status = 'cancelled')

input: Which providers have treated patients from every city on file? Show their full names.
output: SELECT p.full_name FROM providers p JOIN appointments a ON a.provider_id = p.id JOIN patients pt ON pt.id = a.patient_id GROUP BY p.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pt.city) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM patients)

input: Which patient or patients have the most appointments? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT pt.first_name, pt.last_name FROM patients pt JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = pt.id GROUP BY pt.id HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments GROUP BY patient_id))

input: Show the ids of appointments booked for the longest procedure on offer.
output: SELECT id FROM appointments WHERE procedure_id IN (SELECT id FROM procedures WHERE duration_minutes = (SELECT MAX(duration_minutes) FROM procedures))

input: Which insurance plans have an average appointment copay above 25? Show the plan names.
output: SELECT pt.insurance_plan FROM appointments a JOIN patients pt ON pt.id = a.patient_id GROUP BY pt.insurance_plan HAVING AVG(a.copay) > 25

input: Which active providers have never had a no-show? Show their full names.
output: SELECT full_name FROM providers WHERE is_active = 1 AND id NOT IN (SELECT provider_id FROM appointments WHERE status = 'no-show')

input: Which patients have seen more than one different provider? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT pt.first_name, pt.last_name FROM patients pt JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = pt.id GROUP BY pt.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.provider_id) > 1

input: Which provider specialties have completed appointments whose procedure base fees total more than 2000? Show the specialty names.
output: SELECT p.specialty FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id JOIN procedures pr ON pr.id = a.procedure_id WHERE a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.specialty HAVING SUM(pr.base_fee) > 2000

input: Which procedures are booked more often than the average booked procedure? Show the procedure names.
output: SELECT pr.name FROM procedures pr JOIN appointments a ON a.procedure_id = pr.id GROUP BY pr.id HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT AVG(n) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments GROUP BY procedure_id))

input: Which rooms hosted appointments on more than fifteen distinct days? Show the room names.
output: SELECT r.name FROM rooms r JOIN appointments a ON a.room_id = r.id GROUP BY r.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT substr(a.scheduled_at, 1, 10)) > 15

input: Which patients had their first ever appointment in January 2026? Show first and last names.
output: SELECT pt.first_name, pt.last_name FROM patients pt JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = pt.id GROUP BY pt.id HAVING MIN(a.scheduled_at) LIKE '2026-01%'

input: Which cities have more patients than the average number of patients per city? Show the city names.
output: SELECT city FROM patients GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM patients)

input: Which patients have an appointment with a provider who is no longer active? Show distinct first and last names.
output: SELECT DISTINCT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM appointments WHERE provider_id IN (SELECT id FROM providers WHERE is_active = 0))

input: Which rooms have hosted appointments for more than one specialty of provider? Show the room names.
output: SELECT r.name FROM rooms r JOIN appointments a ON a.room_id = r.id JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id GROUP BY r.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.specialty) > 1
